newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends higher, Dec hits 15-week high.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends higher, Dec hits 15-week high.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed higher for the second consecutive day amid brisk speculative buying that carried the benchmark December contract to a 15-week high, traders said.
Decmber rose to 77.65 cents, its highest level since hitting 78.15 cents on March 12, before closing at 77.44, up 0.51. The rest of the board finished 0.45 to 0.65 cent firmer.
The trade remained a steady seller of the December contract and a buyer of call options.
"The trade might be buying options but they are also selling the board," a floor source said, adding that the steady selling could limit further gains.
Firm technical resistance was pegged at 77.70 to 77.95 cents basis December.

Market sources said a positive export report on Thursday could lift prices slightly higher, but added that prices should remain steady on Friday ahead of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's official planted area estimate.
Market sources said expectations for a cut from the March estimate of 14.485 million acres in 1997/98 has lent fundamental support to the recent rally.
"The market is anticipating a bullish report and pricing it in now," a trader said. "If we don't get a bullish number we could be down very, very sharply."

Prices could be in for a sharp correction regardless of Monday's report. One trader noted that the market has not managed to hold a significant move higher or lower without reversing within four days, for the life of the December contract.
Open interest in the July contract stood at 3,323 lots as of Monday, down 4,919 lots from the previous session.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 23,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's official 21,688 lots.
